title: MISSIONS: THE FUTURE OF THE CHURCH
mv: And He said to them, "Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.
mvp: “And He said to them, "Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.” Mark 16:15 (NKJV)
assignment: Write out five (5) reasons to show that it is more important to multiply the labourers than to continue to labour all alone in God’s vineyard (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: The church is intrinsically missional, created to participate in God's redemptive agenda to redeem the world. As followers of Christ, we are called to fulfil the Great Commission, which is to make disciples of all nations (Matthew 28:19-20). If the church exists to serve God's purpose, then its future lies in its commitment to missions. God's purpose is to bring all people together in Christ (Ephesians 1:9-10), and missions is the means by which this purpose is fulfilled.

The future of the church depends on successfully raising new generations of faithful disciples and preparing them for missions work. This requires the church to be intentional about spiritually engaging and equipping young men and women for the work of the gospel (Colossians 2:1-8; 2Timothy 3:16-17). Jesus' command to "teach all nations" implies a process of discipling, mentoring, and equipping others to do the same. To multiply the labourers, discipleship should be taken seriously. As we disciple others, we can help them become co-labourers in God's harvest field (Philippians 4:1-3). The Greek word for "teach" in Matthew 28:19 primarily means "disciple." The ultimate goal of a missional church is not just evangelism but discipleship; people get saved through evangelism but become Christ-like and prepared for ministry through discipleship.

“Missions” is a universal vocation for God's children, regardless of age, background, or socio-economic status. Nobody is left out, and everyone must be involved in this noble endeavour (3John 1:5-8). In Matthew 20:1-7, we see that the master has an assignment for everyone, and He expects us to work diligently in His vineyard. Therefore, we must not stay idle but rather actively involve ourselves in missions work (Luke 8:1-3). We can sow the seeds of prayer towards missions, release our resources for missions, and demonstrate our love for God by actively participating in missions (Philippians 4:14-17; Colossians 4:2-4). As the Bible says, "Go ye also into the vineyard" (Matthew 20:7). By doing so, we can fulfil our purpose as followers of Christ.
‘Missions’ is not just a programme or activity of the church; it is the very essence of its existence. The survival of the church depends on its commitment to the Great Commission.

How can believers be involved in missions?
